# 1.2.109 - The Class Trial's entry and the verdict's cut-in, the clock's turns with a direction, the Investigation's flashes and the body's flicker, the day's boards and the school's mood, the Spectator; on Daggerheart 2.12 the GM draws the players' rolls again

Stages E61, E62 (`with` E61), E92 (`with` E62) and E94 (`with` E92), one release; and E76b, the roll fix for
Daggerheart 2.12 that E76 (1.2.106) left out, from the E76 line. 1.2.108 (E73, E99) was released from another tree
and is merged in here (f46f5bc4); its own commits are 1.2.108's. Its range is v1.2.108 (4dfac3a9) to the release
commit: at e730d5c6, eighty-two commits, nine of them merges (`git rev-list --count` and `--merges --count` over
4dfac3a9..e730d5c6). Thirty-six are on the E61/E62 work line's branch, 9c36b17d to aa8771c5 (one of them the merge
60493865, which took the 1.2.107 line into the branch), merged as 112e2ea3, 08ba24e1, 7872146d and cb95a366; eight are
on the E76 line's branch, eb207826 to 1d62225e, merged as 124eac28; twenty-four are on E92's branch, 0a0f211c to
ce1ffadb (one of them the merge 63d3c9c1), merged as 046926ef. Fourteen stand on the 1.2.109 line itself
(`--first-parent`): those six merges, f46f5bc4, which merges main at 1.2.108, and seven commits - 9c804f93 renumbers
E92's live checks, f09132cc the handbooks' version tags, 9fc9fa52 gives a Spectator its end-of-day board, ad46b385
holds E92's two censuses to 1.2.108's code, e9e8e549 corrects the texts a re-read at ad46b385 found stale (the GM
handbook's Sound section among them), fe824416 one word of E92's STATUS that e9e8e549 left, and e730d5c6 holds
R812's reading against a timing race in that test (the base's one red CI run; Checked). On top come ad6b9011,
which writes this train's rows in tools/stages.json (E94 `with` E92 and planned 1.2.109; E61, E62 and E94 `touches`
[]), and the release commit. The release's first CI run (43287328954, on the gate's record b30f9444) was red
in scenario 12-social and twenty tier-2 tests; a0da54e6 and e6aaac31 fix them (below, "Fixed after the release's
first CI run"), and the gate's record is written again after them. In plain words:

- **The Class Trial's entry.** Every road into the Class Trial now plays one short full-screen entry on every screen
  at the table: the curtain closes, the title **CLASS TRIAL** stands on it with the chapter's line, and it opens onto
  the trial, 3.4 seconds in all. Under Stained Glass the panes on screen stay where they are and the gap between them
  closes with new panes of the same glass, each sliding out from behind the edge of the glass beside it; under
  Monokuma Legacy two black lids close and open.
- **The verdict's cut-in.** The GM's verdict card plays a cut-in on every screen (3.7 seconds): the sentenced
  student's portrait and name, the votes as counted, the stamp **GUILTY** / **WINNY** when the class got it right or
  **NOT GUILTY** / **NIEWINNY** when not, and the card's sentence. It shows only what the card already says.
- **The clock's turns.** Each change of the clock turns the curtain in its own direction (an hour forward from the
  top, a new day and a rewind from the bottom, the Eclipse in from the centre and out inward); the Investigation
  begins with six flashes of panes, each with the new sound **Pane flash**; when a body is announced, the seams and
  the pulse flicker four times.
- **The day's boards.** When Night turns to Morning, every screen first shows the end-of-day board for about six
  seconds: what you did that day, what the whole school saw and **the school's mood** - Calm, Uneasy or Close to
  spilling. It shows no Hope or Despair. The mood weighs the students' Hope against the Monocubs' Hope, Monokuma's
  Despair and the Overflow; it is only a word, and the numbers behind it stay hidden. Then the start-of-day
  board, about five seconds: the day, the chapter, the hour and the cast, the dead greyed in their place with "we
  remember", and the GM's **morning line** when the GM wrote one (Edit campaign, **Next morning's line**).
- **Cards in the middle of the screen.** The day summary and the card that announces a body now stand in the middle
  of the screen, over the windows, until you touch them. The day summary waits for the clock's turn, and its rows come
  in one after another.
- **The Spectator.** The GM can make a player a **Spectator** (Students window, Role **Spectator** / **Widz**): it
  watches and does not play. It has no chat, takes no actions and counts nowhere. It sees every project's name and
  progress, secret ones too, but not a secret project's description. Other players do not see its token; the GM sees it
  faint, at 30 % of its opacity. Its microphone is off; a button on its voice tile lets it talk with the other
  Spectators. At the day's end it sees only the end of the day and the school's mood.
- **Esc, reduced motion and a switch.** Esc skips the entry, the cut-in, a turn or a board on that screen only; with reduced motion a still
  frame stands instead of the motion; the game's settings have **Full-screen sequences** (Sekwencje na cały ekran),
  on by default, to turn them off for the whole table.
- **Daggerheart 2.12.** On Daggerheart 2.12, 1.2.106 stopped the GM drawing the players' rolls and threw them in
  each player's browser. 1.2.109 carries the module's marks through Daggerheart 2.12's new roll road, so the GM draws
  them again, and reads a roll's outcome where 2.12 now keeps it. Measured headless against copies of Daggerheart
  2.12.8's own code, not at a table.

Nothing in this version ran at a real table or on a Foundry server; what was measured was measured headless, in
Chromium on the module's glass harness (the module's stylesheets, not Foundry's), or against the harness's copies of
Daggerheart's code. Below, an R number names one of the module's own tests (`game.drpg.runTests()`), and a scenario
one of the headless harness's multi-browser runs. The gaps are in Not in this release, Known gaps and Checked.

## Before installing

- **Every screen at the table plays the new sequences by default** (E61, E62, E94): the trial's entry, the verdict's
  cut-in, the clock's turns, the Investigation's flashes, the body's flicker and the two boards of the day. A GM who
  wants none of them turns **Full-screen sequences** off before the session; each player can skip one with Esc. The
  cards in the middle of the screen (below) are not under the switch: they stand there with it off too. While the
  switch is on, the Night's own day summary is not put up at the roll-over to Morning: the end-of-day board takes its
  place (day-summary.mjs `nightFoldsIntoBoard`, R3724).
- **New world setting `sequences`** (E61 C1): **Full-screen sequences** / **Sekwencje na cały ekran**, a Boolean, on
  by default, in the DRPG Settings window's game section (the GM list; R3702). Off: neither the entry nor the cut-in
  is drawn, and their two sounds still play (Q-E61-2's default, R3701); no Investigation flash and no flicker, and the
  curtain turns from the centre as before 1.2.109 (R3712); no day's boards, and so no day chimes (R3715). Its hint names
  the entry, the verdict, the clock's turns and flashes and the day boards, and says only the trial's and the verdict's
  sounds play (e1154c1d, shortened in 6b98f6c9).
- **New Sound rows**, in the Sound window's incident category, with English and Polish text: **The Class Trial
  starts** (`trialStart`, Start rozprawy), **Verdict cut-in** (`verdictCut`, Cut-in werdyktu), **Pane flash**
  (`paneFlash`, Błysk szyby, its pitch varied), **Start of the day** (`dayStart`, Początek dnia) and **End of the day**
  (`dayEnd`, Koniec dnia). The row the vote's count plays (`verdict`) is relabelled **The vote's result** (Wynik
  głosowania); its key is kept, so a saved sound map keeps its file (Q-E61-7's default).
- **The verdict card carries one new flag** (E61 C5, verdict.mjs): `verdictCut: { sentenced, right }`, the sentenced's
  ids and whether the class got it right - what the card's words already say; never the Blackened (R3707). A card
  posted before 1.2.109 has none, and a client that loads after a card was posted plays nothing.
- **New GM field** (E94 C1): **Next morning's line** / **Zdanie na następny poranek** in Edit campaign, kept only in
  that GM's browser (client setting `morningLineDraft`) until the next morning starts.
- **The clock carries three new fields** (E94 C1, C3, C4): the morning line, when the day began (`dayStartedAt`, R3725)
  and the school's mood as a word; the Overflow's numbers are never written there (R3723, world-secrets).
- **Two cards stand in the middle of the screen** (E62 C5): the day summary and the body's card, over the windows
  until touched, for everyone, with **Full-screen sequences** on or off (popup.mjs `centre` reads no switch; only the
  summary's wait for the clock's turn does, `summaryDelay`). A chat card asks for this with a new flag, `popupCentre`, honoured only on a GM's card
  (R3729).
- **New Role, Spectator** (E92): a GM's flag on a character (`spectator`), set in the Students window; a Spectator's
  own "Talk with the Spectators" switch is a flag on its User. Nothing changes until a GM sets the Role. Setting or
  clearing it writes more than the flag: monokuma.mjs `setSpectator` runs projects.mjs `seeAsSpectators`, which takes
  an account that stopped being a Spectator off every secret project it does not build and reseals every secret
  project, so each Spectator's account stands as an observer in that project's ownership map (projects-secrecy.mjs
  `ownershipMap`; a world setting every browser holds); clearing it first runs fog.mjs `forgetSpectatorMap`, which
  writes the rooms of the class's map the character never found itself as unfound for it - unticked cells a GM's Fog
  tab shows.
- **No world migration.** Nothing is renamed or rewritten at load. The new setting is born on at the first load.
- **What players can now see**: the sequences above, on their own screens. The cut-in reads only the GM's card and
  the public record (`trialProgress`, the count already public since the count's card): a Blackened planted beside the
  sentenced is nowhere in it, and a player's message with the same flags plays nothing (R3706). The start-of-day board
  shows a student as dead by the published flag alone: a death the GMs keep is not shown as one (R3714). A client that
  loads after the event plays nothing (Q-E61-1 and Q-E94-4, defaults). The end-of-day board shows a player only that
  player's own actions and the school's public cards (R3721). A Spectator sees every project's name and progress, secret
  ones included, never a secret project's description (R3867). A student's browser reads in a secret project's
  ownership map which account is a Spectator's observer of it, as it reads any viewer's (docs/dev/e92/STATUS.md).
- **Flashes**: the Investigation's entry flashes six groups of panes in about 2.4 seconds and the body's flicker dims
  four times; neither sequence alone flashes more than 3 times in any second (R3710 reads the six onsets and the four
  each alone), and nothing flashes under reduced motion. Both on one screen at once is read by no test, and the share
  of the screen one group covers was not measured (Known gaps).
- **On Daggerheart 2.12 the GM draws the players' rolls again** (E76b, 2f8e48b9). 1.2.106 left the GM's draw off on
  any Daggerheart whose `rollTrait` builds a MoveContext, threw every player's roll in the player's browser and
  whispered the GMs once per version. 1.2.109 draws them on such a build where the MoveContext Daggerheart offers keeps
  the caller's event (read off its constructor), as Daggerheart 2.12.8's does; there the whisper and the console line
  no longer come. On a build whose MoveContext keeps no event, or whose `rollTrait` cannot be read, 1.2.106's behaviour
  stands (R3602). On Daggerheart up to 2.10 nothing changes (R3604, R3606).
- **`module.json`**: unchanged but for the version. No `verified` is raised without a check at a real table:
  Foundry `verified` 14.365, Daggerheart `verified` 2.6.5.
- **The handbooks** (English and Polish): the GM handbook's section 15.3 (the entry, the cut-in, Esc, reduced motion, the
  switch), section 4 (the clock's turns and the day's boards) and section 17, Sound (the five new rows in its Incident
  row, a paragraph on when each plays and that the boards and the flash are silent with the switch off, and "the
  verdict" now "the vote's result"; e9e8e549), the player handbook's "Full-screen moments", and the Spectator in both.

## The Class Trial's entry (E61 C1, C3, C4; rounds 2-5: 8937575c, 8ab51249, 1db3f623, 98e004c1)

Every road into the Class Trial plays one entry on every screen, from the clock's one event (`drpgPhaseChanged`;
R3704: the entry's key is the trial's edge stamp, so a second hearing starts nothing): about a second of closing, the
title **CLASS TRIAL** with the chapter's line from 1400 ms, the opening from 2500 ms, 3.4 s in all
(`scripts/sequence.mjs`).

- **Stained Glass** (1db3f623, 8ab51249): the standing panes keep their place, and the hole they leave closes with new
  panes of the curtain's own kind - convex, of the standing panes' corner count and size range, cut by straight lines
  (`scripts/glass-close.mjs` `fillHole`). Each new pane keeps its size and shape from its first frame and slides out
  from behind an edge it shares with glass already there, along that edge's normal, drawn only inside its own place
  (`slidePlan`, `slideAt`); generations start when the one before is 70 % through, outer first, 860 ms in all. The
  closed curtain is the curtain's own paint (`curtainPaint`) of the whole cut; the opening is the reverse onto the
  trial's cut. The panes' colour turns from the Investigation's blue to the trial's pink in eight batches, outer first.
- **Above 1366x768** (98e004c1, round 5): the new panes keep 1366x768's share of the screen. The standing cut is built
  of fixed pixel sizes, so with them alone the new panes came out half as large at 1920x1080 (a median 1.20-1.33 % of
  the screen against 2.19-2.28 % at 1366x768); now the target grows with the screen's area, the hole is first cut on a
  grid at the curtain's slants, and small pieces at the rim are joined with a neighbour or cut again with it. At
  1366x768 and below the fill is round 4's, pane for pane (10 seeds, GM and player, compared with 1db3f62's file). The
  at-rest cut is not changed.
- **Monokuma Legacy** and wherever no curtain is cut: two black lids with a red edge, the same title, times and sound;
  no glass code runs (R3704).
- **Reduced motion**: a still frame - the closed curtain (or the lids) and the title for 1.5 s (R3705). The room and
  voice tiles are covered for the span and come back with it (R3705).
- Red first: R3703 and R3716 at 8937575 (no `fillHole`), R3718 at 8ab5124 (no `slidePlan` or `slideAt`; the entry
  drew grown insets), R3719 at 1db3f62 ("share ratio 0.489, aspect 0.423 against 0.448"); green at 98e004c. Rounds 1
  and 2 (an affine closed plan; fronts flooding the hole) were replaced on the owner's reviews and are gone.
- Measured, round 4 (the glass harness in headless Chromium, the real cut, 7 sizes 1280x720-2560x1440, GM and
  player): 0 overlapping pairs of panes in each of 92 frames; 0 frames with a pane drawn at another size; every pane
  wholly behind its edge (within 1 px) at its start; every point of a 6 px grid in exactly one pane; 2-4 generations, a
  pane's slide 242-400 ms. Round 5, the same 7-size check: 0 overlaps in 92 frames, 0 frames at another scale, every
  pane behind its edge at its start, 0 gaps and 0 doubles, in all 14 cases. Over eight seeds (Node), the GM's median
  share at 1920x1080 is 0.94 of 1366x768's and the player's 1.04; the median aspect 0.48 at 1920x1080 against 0.45 and
  0.48.

## The verdict's cut-in (E61 C5; 9c36b17d, 64d9bcca, 9daf9d8b, 8937575c)

The GM's verdict card (`createChatMessage`, a message with `verdictAt` from a GM) plays a cut-in on every screen: the
band at 0, the portrait at 250 ms, the votes at 900 ms, the stamp's hit at 1700 ms, the card's sentence at 1950 ms,
the last frame held to 3500 ms, then a 180 ms fade. Variants: **GUILTY** when the class got it right, **NOT GUILTY**
when not, and nobody sentenced (neither portrait nor stamp); two sentenced stand side by side with a stamp each
(Q-E61-3's default). The count's heading and each vote row come in one after another (320 ms each, 90 ms apart, eased),
each bar after its row, and the sentence in 380 ms (8937575c, the owner's review of round 1). Under Stained Glass the
stamp is bone in every variant (gold means Hope alone since E48), so the variant is told by its word. Under reduced
motion the last frame stands for 3 s and nothing animates (R3717). `verdictBoardElement` is the last frame alone, for
E99's summary later.

- Red first: R3706 and R3707 at f22a7e87 by their comments (sequence.mjs absent; no `verdictCut` flag), no run of
  that red quoted; R3717 at 6049386 ("the count's rows came in as one block"), green at 8937575.

## The sequence engine, the table's switch and the sounds (E61 C1, C2; 9c36b17d, d380f7d9, d03c5091, 60493865)

- One start per event, one sequence at a time (a new one or a phase change cuts the running one); Escape in a
  capture listener registered before the module's window handler, taken only while a sequence plays (R3700); Foundry
  tools and Map tools hidden by a body attribute for the span, never collapsed; the notice stack raised over the
  host; the notice tile and the cards where they stood after it (R3700); counters `sequence.*`. A sequence writes no
  setting and no document (R3700).
- The frame times are read in sequence.mjs (`SEQUENCE_TIMES`), not as motion.css tokens: motion.css zeroes its tokens
  under reduced motion, and the still frame must still stand its 1.5 s and 3 s.
- The two sounds play at their frame (the title's, the stamp's), once on each screen; under reduced motion or with the
  switch off at once (R3701).
- d03c5091: the sequences' sizes in clamp() for their viewport host (R60's count 2 -> 6) and the table's lifetimes
  count 37 (R1256). 60493865 (the 1.2.107 line merged into the branch): the switch moved into the window's game
  section, where that line put the GM's settings (R3420, R3702).
- **Counted on each browser** (E61 C6 in part, 463d12ff): sequence.mjs counts each sequence by kind
  (`sequence.<kind>`) beside `sequence.started`, and scenario 63 holds three checks on its own clients: the trial's
  entry played once on each of the GM and p1-p3 from the one Start (A3), none on p4, loaded after it (C2), and the
  verdict's cut-in once on each of gm2 and the four players (G4). Red at 8675f81 (no counter), 74/74 at 463d12ff.
  Not held: a reload during the entry or the cut-in, End the trial during a cut-in, the trial with one E70 mode.

## The clock's turns (E62 C1, C2, C4, C8 part, Q6; 08c4e719, 5dce8f14, 62309451)

- Each change of the clock turns the curtain in its own direction, from one pure planner (`transitionFor`, R3709): an
  hour forward from the top (every forward hour, Q5's default), a new day and a rewind from the bottom, the Eclipse
  in from the centre and out inward (1.4 s), the trial's exit from the centre; the trial's entry is E61's. The clock's
  hooks hand the curtain its direction (`hintTurn`); `turnPlan` takes `how`, `groups` and `delays`, and with none
  turns as before (R3711); `paneOrder` orders the panes from the top, the bottom, the centre, inward or seeded at
  random (R3708). A transition writes no setting and no document (R3712).
- **The Investigation's entry**: six random groups of the panes on screen flash at 0, 360, 900, 1320, 1930 and 2400 ms
  (the owner's mockup MK-R3), each with **Pane flash**, its pitch varied. A recording found that the batches were spaced
  `gap` apart where the plan used these uneven onsets, and Chromium refused the negative duration that made (no turn
  drawn); fixed in 5dce8f14, which R3711 reads.
- **The body's flicker**: when a body is announced (`drpgBodyAnnounced`), the seams and the pulse dim for 220 ms at 0,
  450, 900 and 1350 ms on every browser; under Legacy the clock, status, Despair bar and notice tile light instead; a
  rehearsal's announcement plays nothing (R3713). A fixed 1.6 s, not the sound's length (Q7's default).
- **Esc** ends a running transition on that screen at its end state (`holdEscape`, `skipTurn`; R3713).
- **Two changes of the clock close together** end on the second: its direction handed, the first's later flashes
  dropped, Esc held for the second (R3727, added in E94's commit e1154c1d and stamped E94; not red first - green at
  7bbbd3c and e1154c1, red with `clearFlashes`' line taken out on a scratch run, docs/dev/e62/STATUS.md).
- **The HUD's phase label** slides in from the right when the phase changes, fading in over the turn's length, as the
  time label does; nothing on a page load, for the same phase or under reduced motion (`slidePhase`, R3728; 62309451,
  Q6's default). Red at 6b98f6c by its commit message.
- Red first, by the tests' comments: R3708-R3713 at d03c509 (transitions.mjs absent; no `paneOrder`; `turnPlan` with
  no `how`; no `holdEscape`), no run of that red quoted.

## The centre cards (E62 C5; 8675f81e)

- `showPopup` takes `centre`: the card stands on the middle stage, the one the trial's evidence uses (no history
  button), raised over the windows until touched, and is kept in the history as every card is. A chat card asks for
  it with `popupCentre`, honoured only from a GM's card (R472's census row) (R3729).
- The day summary waits for the clock's turn (`summaryDelay`) and its rows slide in 160 ms apart from 150 ms, none
  under reduced motion (R3730). The body's card stands in the centre for everyone (the plan's Q8 default).
- Red first: R3729 and R3730 at 6230945, by the commit message; no run quoted.

## The start-of-day board (E94 C2; 5131d3b6, f93c9f69, 4987f711, 1262ebe5)

At the Night-to-Morning roll-over (Q-E94-2's default: no new button), on every connected browser, the day's board
rises for about 5 s and goes by itself, Esc earlier: the day, the chapter, the hour and the cast in its order, the
dead by the published flag alone (`isDeceased`), greyed in place with their name and "we remember", never struck
through; the alive count as a ratio, **Alive: 6/8** / **Ocaleli: 6/8**; the GM's morning line only when there is one
(E94 C1, below). Still under reduced motion (5 s), nothing with the switch off (R3715); the chime
**Start of the day**; the board lets the table's clicks through (R3715). It plays over E62's turn from the bottom,
both from the same event.

- Red first: R3714 and R3715 at 3c36fcb by their comments (no `dayStartBoard`, no `playDayStart`). Tiers 0-1 at
  5180954 failed R1157, the plural census ("alive: 6 of 8" put a count before an agreeing word outside a plural
  family); reworded as a ratio in 1262ebe5. The review page's recording found the rise's transform replacing the
  board's centring (half a screen off), fixed in 4987f711, which R3714 reads. f93c9f69: the names wrap at their
  spaces, a wider row.

## The end-of-day board, the morning line and the school's mood (E94 C1, C3, C4; e1154c1d, 6b98f6c9, aa8771c5, 9fc9fa52)

- **The end-of-day board** plays first at the Night-to-Morning roll-over, about 6 s, then the start-of-day board: a
  player sees only its own student's actions of the day, a GM the table's; the module's public cards of the day (no
  whisper, no blind roll); and the mood - no Hope or Despair, the owner's word (R3722, 6b98f6c9). It stays as one card in the notice history and takes the place
  of the Night's own summary while the switch is on (R3721, R3722, R3724).
- **The school's mood**: Calm, Uneasy or Close to spilling, from one share - the living students' Hope over that Hope
  plus the Monocubs' Hope, the Monokumas' Despair and the Overflow count - against config.mjs `MOOD_SHARES` (0.6 and
  0.4, and the mood worked out on the GM who moves the clock: made final by the owner's "Tak" of 12.11, as
  docs/dev/e94/STATUS.md records it); only the word goes out, and a tier-2 test holds the
  stored clock to the word alone (R3723; 6b98f6c9, red at b07dec9 by its commit message).
- **A Spectator's board** (the owner's word, 12.11): the day's heading and the mood's word, nothing else - no rows, no
  public cards, no chapter line; its browser does not read the day's rows (`dayEndBoardFor`; R3868 and scenario 93's
  part "board", both red at 7872146d and green at 9fc9fa52).
- **Shorter texts** (6b98f6c9, the owner's rule): the sequences' hint, the morning line's hint, the quiet day, the five
  sound rows' hints and the handbook paragraphs; the player handbook names no numbers.
- **The morning line**: typed by a GM in Edit campaign, it stays in that GM's browser and reaches the board only when
  Night turns to Morning; then the draft is emptied (R3720).
- **A stray merge marker**: the work line's merge 60493865 left a `=======` line in styles/danganronpa.css that dropped
  the Monokuma Legacy rule for Foundry's notifications; e1154c1d removed it, and R3726 keeps the served files free of
  markers. No release carried it (1.2.107's 235c3210 and 1.2.108's 4dfac3a9 hold none).
- **More room under the chapter line** (aa8771c5, the owner's word of 12.11 on the review page): on the end-of-day
  board alone, 22 of the sequence's units below the chapter line, 12 px -> 31 px at 1366x768, in both themes, English
  and Polish, the board still inside the screen (R3731, red at 463d12f by its commit message).
- Red first: R3720-R3726 at 7bbbd3c, green at e1154c1 (docs/dev/e94/STATUS.md, no run of the red quoted); R3722, R3723
  and the tier-2 test again at b07dec9 (6b98f6c9's message).

## The Spectator (E92; 0a0f211c..ce1ffadb, 9fc9fa52, ad46b385)

- **Who it is**: a character a GM marks **Spectator** in the Students window. It is no student: no vote, trial,
  incident, room count, Hope or Calls (R3850-R3852). Every player action through the GM is refused for it ("A
  Spectator takes no actions.", R3865), the zone modes' side pick and Scrum thesis from 1.2.108 included (ad46b385).
- **Its chat**: blocked. Its own browser refuses the message ("A Spectator has no chat."), no browser draws one, and the
  primary GM removes it (scenario 93).
- **What it sees**: every room the class found, every token, and every project's name and progress, secret ones too;
  not a secret project's description (R3855, R3856, R3867).
- **Its token**: hidden from the other players; on the GM's canvas at 0.3 of its opacity, nothing else (R3866). It moves
  by dragging its token; whether a wall stops that drag on v14 is not tried (LIVE-E92-02).
- **Its voice**: the microphone is held in every phase (R3853); **Talk with the Spectators** / **Go back to your room**

## Rolls drawn by the GM on Daggerheart 2.12 again (E76b, 2f8e48b9)

- **What a GM and a player see**: on Daggerheart 2.12 (as read and run against 2.12.8's code), a player's action roll
  is drawn by the GM again, as on 2.10: the module's roll window opens with the module's settings, the claim finds the
  roll by its mark, the Loaded Die and a statistic a GM picked reach the roll, and the module's card, Hope and the
  Calls read the outcome as before. The once-a-version whisper of 1.2.106 ("... the players' rolls are thrown in
  their own browsers and not drawn by the GM ...") no longer comes on such a build.
- **Why it broke**: Daggerheart 2.12's `actor.rollTrait` builds a MoveContext from the options it is given
  (actor.mjs:727-743, 2.12.8), which keeps only the properties it names and sets `dialog` to {} (move-context.mjs:21-):
  the module's `drpgActionRoll`, the claim's nonce, `LOADED_DIE`, `TRAIT_BY_GM` and `dialog.configure` never reached
  the build. It keeps the caller's own event object (`this.event ??= data.event`). And 2.12 moved a roll's outcome from
  `config.roll` to the evaluated Roll (`config.evaluated`).
- **The fix**: a new leaf, `scripts/roll-marks.mjs`. `carryMarks` registers the marks against the options' own event
  (a WeakMap, one object a roll, so two rolls in flight cannot take each other's); `adoptMarks` puts them back on the
  config where Daggerheart's build starts - in roll-draw.mjs's `drawnBuild` before the draw reads them, and in the
  `daggerheart.preRollDuality` hook, which Daggerheart's `buildConfigure` calls before the window opens and the roll
  is made; a mark already on the config stands. action-pipeline.mjs carries them on its one `actor.rollTrait` call.
  `fillRollFacts` writes a 2.12 roll's total, formula, dice, critical, Hope and Fear faces and duality where 2.10 wrote
  them, only where missing, so the module's readers read them as before; critical.mjs reads the critical off
  `config.evaluated` where it is there. roll-draw.mjs `seamFor`: a `rollTrait` that builds a MoveContext is "ok" where
  the MoveContext Daggerheart offers (`game.system.api.data.actions`) keeps the event, read off its constructor's
  text; "changed" where it keeps none, none is offered, or `rollTrait` cannot be read (R3602, revised).
- **Red first**, on the harness's 2.12.8 copies without the fix (ca44459 + C3d, a detached worktree): R3602 measured
  its last case "changed" where "ok" was expected; R3604 and R3606 threw (no roll-marks.mjs); R3605 measured
  `{"hope":1,"stress":-1}` for a critical where the guide's 2 Hope was expected; scenarios 20-crit-hope 3/6,
  83-roll-integrity 53/110, 40-flow 65/88. Green: R217, R3602, R3604, R3605, R3606; 20-crit-hope 6/6, 83-roll-integrity
  110/110, 40-flow 88/88, 88-flow-length 26/26. Mutants (tier 1), each KILLED: the MoveContext's event check dropped
  (R3602); the critical read off `config.roll` only (R3605); `fillRollFacts` writing over 2.10's facts (R3606);
  `adoptMarks` leaving the window's configure, and writing over a mark already there (R3604).
- No lang key added or changed.

## Fixed after the release's first CI run (a0da54e6, e6aaac31)

- **A GM's Grant on Daggerheart 2.12 moved no Hope, Stress or Fear** (e6aaac31). The Grant handed Daggerheart's
  resource step the outcome where 2.10 reads it (`config.roll`); 2.12.8 reads it on `config.evaluated`. It now carries
  both. Red first: the suite's three Grant tests read Hope 0 where 1 and 3 were expected.
- **A roll the GM drew could not be written to its message on 2.12** (e6aaac31). 2.12 hangs the thrown roll on its
  own options, so the roll's JSON was circular; the GM's draw now gives the roll a copy of its options without it.
  The harness had hidden this: it dropped a key it could not write without a word. It now writes a roll to JSON as
  Foundry does, and the new tier-2 test "a roll the GM drew is written on its message as JSON that rebuilds it"
  measured the circular JSON before the fix. That a table's Foundry refused such a message is read from its source,
  not measured.
- **The harness read 2.10's shapes** (e6aaac31): a 2.12 MoveContext's options through its own `toJSON`, an effect's
  changes on `system.changes`, and four tests' readings of a roll's total on `config.evaluated`. One case of the
  fromData test, a renamed plain die, cannot hold on 2.12 (its `fromData` names that die from a field 2.12 no longer
  writes), and is dropped with that reason.
- **The clock's three new fields had no defaults** (a0da54e6): the day's start, the school's mood and the morning line
  (E94) were missing from the clock's defaults, so a test's restore could not take them away. They are null now,
  which every reader already reads as not known. E37-T10 waits for the day's summary, which since E62 comes after a
  short pause.
- Runs: tiers 0-1 1305 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped; scenarios 12-social, 83 and 33 green; the six clock tests and the
  thirteen roll tests green by name. The rest of tier 2 under the stricter harness is this commit's CI run.

  entry at 1366x768 and 1920x1080 in both themes, as GM and as player, on a real Foundry v14. Written at round 4, it

  like 1366x768's).
- **The cost of building the entry's pieces** (`entryPieces`, once, before the closing), as docs/dev/e61/STATUS.md
  measured it headless on 4 cores: 110-429 ms of main thread in round 2, 125-395 ms in round 3, and 134-186 ms on the
  harness page (its "Blockers"). No figure is recorded for rounds 4 and 5. LIVE-E61-01 (AUDIT 500) carries these three
  figures since e9e8e549; the 162-611 ms it quoted before, which entered with 7f9952ef's text and which no commit
  message or STATUS.md measurement carries, was removed there. None is a table's.
- **New panes outside the standing panes' range**: 0-4 a screen in round 5's 7-size check (round 3 read 0-2), each in a
  crack, wedge or notch between standing panes. R3703 is loosened for one case: on its 1600x900 cut it allows one new
  pane out of range, a 630 px² chip in a notch that no cut through its neighbours' corners or edges splits into two
  panes in range; its 1366x768 and 1440x900 cuts hold none.
- **The at-rest cut is not scaled**: above 1366x768 the standing panes are smaller in share of the screen (1.19 %
  against 2.27 % at 1920x1080); only the entry's new panes follow 1366x768's proportions. One draw swings by about a
  tenth (in Chromium, one seed each: GM 2.14 % against 2.09 % at 1366x768, player 2.45 % against 1.76 %).
- **The review pages' frame strips are drawn on a held clock** with the module's own `slideAt`, not filmed: a
  real-time headless recording at 1920x1080 caught only 2-3 frames of the closing.
- **The lead's widths** are read from the code (`paintGlass`'s 1.2, 0.5 and 0.7 px), not measured in pixels.
- **The microphone** while a sequence covers the voice tile (3.4 s and 3.7 s): LIVE-E61-08 (AUDIT 501).
- **The flashes' share of the screen**: the Investigation's groups are held to 3 onsets a second (R3710), but the
  share of the screen one group covers, which the plan meant to measure at 393x852 against WCAG 2.3.1's flash limit,
  was not measured.
- **Two flash sequences on one screen**: transitions.mjs `onBodyAnnounced` adds its four flicker timers without
  clearing the Investigation's (only the next change of the clock clears them), so a body announced in the first

  **R812's red, read** (the coordinator's investigation, 12.11.2026; e730d5c6): a timing race in R812's own test, not
  in the module. voice-client.mjs's self-check runs every 45 s on its own timer from `ready`; a run landing inside
  R812's 50 ms "own leave" window sees a Room that is not live with nobody moving it, treats it as a drop, shows the
  card and starts reconnect step 1, which the row forbids. About 50 ms in 45 s: about one R812 run in 900, and R812
  runs four times in each shard-1 job; none of 159 shard-1 jobs in CI runs 327-512 failed on it, and runs 512 and
  Release 96 on the same tree passed. Forced alignment (the leave 10 ms before the timer's next run) made the suite's
  own R812 fail 2 of 2 on the "own leave" row (1 card, `{retry: true, step: 1, waiting: true}`; that log keeps only
  that row); a copy of R812's body, not lined up, passed 5 of 5, and lined up failed on that row alone.
  Run 513's own results file could not be fetched (its storage host is refused by this machine's proxy), so its row
  is inferred by reproduction, not read. The fix, e730d5c6 (cherry-picked from 86f0b559, scripts/voice-client.mjs and
  scripts/tests-tier1.mjs only): the timer calls `selfCheckTick`, which does nothing while `holdSelfCheck(true)` holds
  it; `selfCheck()` by name is unchanged and nothing at the table holds the timer (only R812 calls `holdSelfCheck`), so
  the table's behaviour is unchanged; R812 holds the timer for its reading and runs the tick itself right after the
  leave, so the race becomes a fixed reading (red at the parent 2 of 2, green 2 of 2). That pair measures the test's own
  hold: at the parent the new row's tick is `selfCheck` itself, which reads a Room left disconnected after a leave this
  browser asked for as a drop; here the row reads that a held tick does nothing. "Not in the module" is read from the
  code, not measured at a table (LIVE-E19-01). 86f0b559 is a local commit of the investigation and was never pushed;
  e730d5c6 is the one in this release. Checks on 4dfac3a9 with the fix
  (the investigation's): the quick gate green twice, tiers 0-1 "1252 passed, 0 failed", shard 1/8 as CI runs it green
  21/21 (its suite "1255 passed, 0 failed"). On e730d5c6: `node run-tests.mjs --tier 1 --only R812` twice under the
  harness lock, each "1 tests ran" and "2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 red" (R812 and the runner's own "tier 0/1
